Theme

Civic life: news, government & the law

witness noun

also eyewitness, witnesses, testify, bear witness, be called as a witness, step forward as a witness, trustworthy witness, character witness, give evidence against

classical

Plaut. Truc. 489
Cic. Phil. 2.8: quō mē teste convincēs? (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 192, 197, 408

testis, testis m./f.

noun, third declension

To call a witness, testem citāre (Cic. Verr. 2.2.146; M-O s.v. subpoena); to come forward as a witness, testis prōdīre (Traupman 197).

Other words

  • oculātus testis — eyewitness

    phrase: oculātus, oculāta, oculātum (having eyes) with testis · also used · classical · Plaut. Truc. 489; Traupman 192, 195; M-O s.v. eyewitness; Traupman 312

    Plautus’s phrase, set against aurītī, those who have only heard.

  • arbiter, arbitrī m. — an onlooker: someone present who sees or overhears

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 15.16a; Cic. Off. 3.112: remōtīs arbitrīs (Lewis & Short)

    The witness who happens to be there, not one called to court: remōtīs arbitrīs, with no one by.

  • testimōnium dīcere — testify, give testimony

    phrase: testimōnium, testimōniī n. (testimony) with dīcere · also used · classical · Cic. Rosc. Am. 102: testimōnium in aliquem dīcere (Lewis & Short); Traupman 195

    Against someone, in aliquem; for someone, prō aliquō (Traupman 197).

  • testor, testārī, testātus sum — testify, bear witness

    also used · classical · Lewis & Short s.v. testor: “very rare, and not in Cic.” in this sense; Traupman 197

    In the sense “testify” rare and poetic (Lewis & Short); its common sense is “call to witness”. Prose says testimōnium dīcere.

  • advocātus, advocātī m. — a supporter in court; character witness

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Traupman 289

    Classically one called in to support a party in court, by advice or presence (Lewis & Short); Traupman uses it for a character witness.

Examples

  • plūris est oculātus testis ūnus quam aurītī decem

    one eyewitness is worth more than ten who have only heardPlaut. Truc. 489

  • narrō tibi, haec loca venusta sunt, abdita certē et, sī quid scrībere velīs, ab arbitrīs lībera

    I tell you, this place is lovely: hidden, certainly, and free of onlookers, if you want to writeCic. Att. 15.16a

  • testis prōdīre

    to step forward as a witnessTraupman 192, 197

  • contestārī

    to be called as a witnessTraupman 197; Lewis & Short s.v. contestor (passive sense)

  • testis locuplēs

    a trustworthy witnessTraupman 197; cf. Cic. Off. 3.10 (Lewis & Short s.v. locuplēs)

  • testimōnium dīcere in aliquem

    to give evidence against someoneTraupman 195

  • advocātus (advocāta)

    a character witness (one who supports a party in court)Traupman 194

See also trial, court.
